mine: of the remnant of the Rephaim
note: Hebrew ha-repha'im is the name of an ancient people (cf. 2:11, 20); the KJV renders it "giants".

kjv: which was called the land of giants
mine: All that Bashan is called the land of Rephaim
note: Again 'erets repha'im, "land of the Rephaim"; the Hebrew also has a present "is called" (yiqqare'), a parenthetical note by the narrator.
The Hebrew places "the Bashan" as the object renamed (vayyiqra' otam ... et-ha-bashan chavvot ya'ir); the KJV fuses it into a compound place name.

kjv: half the valley, and the border
mine: with the middle of the wadi as a boundary
note: Hebrew tokh ha-nachal u-gevul means "the middle of the wadi and (as) border", i.e. the boundary ran down the riverbed; "half the valley" misreads tokh.
Hebrew 'ashdot is a common noun "slopes, mountain-sides" (cf. Josh 10:40); the KJV transliterates it as part of a place name.
